Subject: Air-gapped VPC topology review for Acme Analytics (control plane / data plane)

Hi all,

Attaching the first-pass topology diagram and a deployment matrix for Acme's private (air-gapped) VPC deployment. This is the configuration we promised after the security workshop last week. Key goals:
- Control plane fully private, customer-managed endpoints (no public control plane IPs).
- Data plane in customer VPC with strict egress controls (only to Redwoods peered endpoints over private connectivity).
- Support for customer HSM/KMS and on-prem registry for container images.

Files attached: redwood-airgap-topology-v1.png (diagram), deployment-matrix-acme.xlsx (roles, ports, and firewall rules). Also shared the diagram in Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-airgap-diagram

High-level questions for review:
1) Does the control-plane placement satisfy Acme's no-internet requirement?
2) Are the proposed subnets / NAT / bastion model acceptable for their SOC 2 control set?
3) Any concerns with our proposed fallback (dedicated NAT with strict egress to Redwoods egress endpoint over VPC peering)?

Please reply with inline comments. Dev — can you validate the kernel/quantization binary distribution approach for an air-gapped registry? Marissa — can you draft a short runbook for day-2 ops once we lock the topology? Samir / Lena — please confirm customer constraints (egress, KMS HSM integration) if anything is missing.

Thanks,

--

Thanks Laura — quick pass from infra. Inline notes below and a few open items.

Inline:
> Control plane fully private, customer-managed endpoints (no public control plane IPs).
- Confirmed: plan uses private ENIs and an internal ALB in the customer control plane VPC. We should explicitly call out that the control plane must be in a subnet with route table entries only to the peering attachment and the customer-managed NAT (no IGW).

> Data plane in customer VPC with strict egress controls (only to Redwoods peered endpoints over private connectivity).
- OK, but need to define the CIDR ranges we will accept on the Redwoods side. I'll attach a small CIDR proposal in the matrix (see deployment-matrix-acme.xlsx).

Open items / risks:
- Container image distribution: air-gapped registry required. We have two options: 
  1) Customer-run registry + image signing (recommended).
  2) Periodic offline sync via hardware transfer (edge case).
- Kernel/binary updates for optimized runtime: we need a secure mechanism for signed artifacts. Is Acme OK with S3-compatible object storage in their VPC for artifact hosting? That would let us pull artifacts over private connectivity.
- Health-checking / outage visibility: without public endpoints, our SREs will need a push-based heartbeat or a contained tracer to surface incidents. We should add a heartbeat agent that can push to a Redwoods ingest endpoint over the private peering.

I will add port-level detail to the spreadsheet and mark the firewall rules that require customer approval.

-Dev

Subject: Re: Air-gapped VPC topology review for Acme Analytics (control plane / data plane)

Laura / Dev / Marissa — thanks for the diagram and matrix. A few clarifications from Acme's side:

1) No public egress: All egress must be blocked except to specific Redwoods peer VPC CIDRs (we will provide an allowlist). No IGW in the control plane VPC and no public IPs on control-plane instances.

2) KMS/HSM: We run an on-prem HSM and must retain key material. Integration should be via a private endpoint that our security team will publish. We cannot share KMS keys; Redwood should support Bring-Your-Own-Key patterns.

3) Image registry: We will run a registry in our environment (Harbor) and will provide image pull credentials scoped to the nodes. Signed images are required; we have a Notary/v2 pipeline.

4) Auditing: We require audit logs for control-plane API calls forwarded to our SIEM. Can Redwood optionally forward control plane audit events (sanitized) to an S3 bucket in our VPC over the peering? If not possible, we need a push model.

5) Failover: In the event of network partition, we need explicit behavior documented — for example, fallback to local inference only (no model downloads), and a well-defined operator escalation path.

We are OK with the proposed bastion and private ALB. I will upload our firewall allowlist and HSM endpoint information into the HubSpot integration doc (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890).
